papers.title: The washing fraction: An overlooked source of molecular information obtained during SPME experiment.
papers.authors: Treder N, Zhu X, Leszczyńska D, Bo T, Kwok T, Pawliszyn J
papers.abstract:
The molecular processes occurring at the interface between biocompatible solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coatings and biological tissue remain poorly understood. The routine post-extraction washing step provides an opportunity to recover and characterize molecules associated with this interface before analytes retained in the extraction phase are desorbed.
In this study, washing fractions generated after 30 min of extraction from bovine skeletal-muscle tissue slices using acupuncture-needle SPME probes coated with C18, self-wettable HLB (wHLB), weak anion-exchange (WAX), or phenylboronic acid (PBA) phases were analyzed by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing with UV and mass spectrometric detection (icIEF-UV/MS) for intact-protein profiling and by liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) for metabolomic and lipidomic profiling. Protein analysis revealed several putative skeletal-muscle protein matches in washing fractions obtained with both WAX and PBA coatings, despite their distinct extraction chemistries, demonstrating coating-dependent recovery of tissue-derived proteins during washing. Washing multiple needles in a fixed volume increased the number of detected intact protein masses, improving protein-profile coverage. Metabolomic and lipidomic profiling revealed coating-dependent differences in the distributions of molecular features between the washing and desorption fractions, demonstrating their distinct molecular compositions. In particular, for C18-coated probes, the washing fraction provided complementary information on relatively polar molecular features that were weakly represented or absent in the corresponding desorption fraction.
These findings establish the routinely discarded SPME washing fraction as an additional source of molecular information complementary to conventional desorption. Analysis of both fractions may therefore expand molecular coverage from a single sampling event without requiring additional tissue sampling.

papers.title: Yiqi Jiedu formula suppresses nasopharyngeal carcinoma growth in association with glycerophospholipid metabolism remodeling: An integrated metabolomics and lipidomics study.
papers.authors: Zhou M, Wu Y, Chen S, Liang R, Lin T, Liu J et al.
papers.abstract:
Yiqi Jiedu formula (YQJDF), a classical traditional Chinese medicine prescription, has been used in the clinical management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Although its therapeutic potential has been indicated by clinical experience, the molecular mechanisms through which it reprograms the intratumoral lipid metabolism remain uncharacterized.
This study aimed to systematically elucidate the antitumor mechanisms of YQJDF by profiling lipid metabolic alterations in tumor tissues through an integrated approach combining non-targeted metabolomics and lipidomics, and identify and validate the key enzymatic regulators of lipid metabolism modulated by the formula.
Non-targeted metabolomics was first performed to map globally altered metabolic pathways in tumor tissues. Subsequently, lipidomics was conducted, with exploratory differential lipids identified using a nominal P value < 0.05 and an OPLS-DA VIP score > 1, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Differential lipids were subjected to hierarchical clustering and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Molecular docking was employed to predict the binding affinity of major formula constituents to key enzymes in enriched pathways, and the expression of candidate targets was validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC).
Non-targeted metabolomics suggested that YQJDF may influence sphingolipid metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, and galactose metabolism. Lipidomics identified 597 exploratory differential lipids, with 179 upregulated and 418 downregulated, of which only PA(P-30:8_18:0), PG(20:4_22:5), and SM(t36:3) remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (FDR < 0.05 and VIP > 1). Clustering analysis showed that these differential lipids were concentrated in phospholipid subclasses. KEGG enrichment analysis pinpointed three core pathways: Choline metabolism in cancer, Efferocytosis, and Glycerophospholipid metabolism. The convergent findings from both omics platforms suggested glycerophospholipid metabolism as a potential pathway associated with treatment. Accordingly, molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities between key formula constituents and critical glycerophospholipid enzymes, including PGS1 and PLA2G4A. IHC showed lower PGS1 and PTDSS1 expression and higher PISD and PLA2G4A expression in the YQ and 3YQ groups compared with the control group. CEPT1 expression was significantly reduced only in the 3YQ group, with a non-significant downward trend in the YQ group.
YQJDF treatment showed antitumor effects and was accompanied by extensive lipid metabolic remodeling in NPC tissues. Glycerophospholipid metabolism may represent an important metabolic pathway associated with YQJDF treatment, and several lipid-metabolism-related enzymes were identified as molecular candidates for further mechanistic investigation. These findings provide a basis for further validation of the role of lipid metabolic alterations in the antitumor response to YQJDF.

papers.title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Liu Y, Li S, Zhang X, Qiang R, Jin F et al.
papers.abstract:
Since surgery can only remove lesions of a larger size visible to the naked eye, the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery is high. In recent years, numerous scholars have found that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment is effective in reducing the recurrence rate of postoperative fibroids, as well as improving the clinical treatment rate, regulating serum hormone levels, reducing plasma viscosity, and promoting the restoration of uterine volume following surgery. Several randomized controlled trials have been undertaken on the prevention and treatment of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids using patented Chinese medicines and self-proposed formulations, such as Guizhi Fuling Pill, Xiaozheng decoction, Xiangleng pill, Zhengjia decoction, Xiaoliu decoction, Guizhi Jiliu pill, Huoxue Huayu formula, Huoxue Xiaozheng decoction, Shugan Sanjie decoction, Gongliuxiao capsule, Hongjin Xiaojie concentrated pill, and Jiawei Guizhi Fuling decoction. However, no study has systematically evaluated Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) in reducing the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery.
This study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of CHM for the prevention of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids, evaluating its efficacy and safety.
A comprehensive search was conducted on PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Information Database (VIP), WanFang Database, and China Biomedical Database (CBM) to identify randomized controlled clinical studies conducted up to March 2025 that examined the efficacy of CHM in treating patients with postoperative uterine fibroids. Two institutes were independently under-selected, and data were extracted and quality assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software 5.4, and forest plots were generated. The quality of evidence was assessed using GRADEpro 3.2.2. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000288).
16 trials were included in this study, and the postoperative recurrence rate after treatment was mainly analyzed. CHM treatment reduces postoperative recurrence rates in patients with uterine fibroids compared to the blank (6 trials, n = 588; OR (odds ratio) = 0.22; 95 % CI (95 % confidence intervals) = 0.14-0.34; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001), conventional western medicine (CWM) (1 trial, n = 80; OR = 0.30; 95 % CI = 0.09-0.93, p = 0.04), and combined CHM with CWM (9 trials, n = 959; OR = 0.29; 95 % CI = 0.19-0.46; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001). In addition, CHM is also effective in improving clinical efficiency, restoring serum sex hormone levels, lowering plasma viscosity, and reducing uterine volume. CHM is generally considered safe, with a low incidence of adverse reactions.
CHM is effective in avoiding recurrence of uterine fibroids after surgery, excelling in terms of overall effectiveness, restoring female hormone levels, improving hemorheological indices, and promoting uterine recovery and safety. However, these findings are preliminary and still need to be validated by higher-quality studies.

papers.title: Fabrication of carbon dots derived from Alangium salviifolium for the sequential sensing Ag+ and S2- and further monitoring of H2S in spoiled food.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Qi X, Yang H, Xu D, Cui T, Dai Q, Chen G et al.
papers.abstract: Given the significant threat posed by heavy metals to ecological system and human health, the development of precise, portable, and on-site analytical technologies is urgently required. Herein, multifunctional carbon dots (A-CDs) derived from the traditional chinese medicine (TCM) were synthesized and exhibited optimal emission at 604 nm excited at 495 nm, with quantum yield (QY) of 18.25%. The A-CDs achieved the cascade determination of Ag+ and S2- via a subsequent "on-off-on" process with LODs of 63.7 nM and 0.98 μM, respectively. Notably, A-CDs portable platform was constructed and enabled on-site quantitative analysis with LODs of 0.83 μM and 1.19 μM, respectively. Leveraging this unique sensing performance, the A-CDs test strips were developed for visual screening of H2S during food spoilage at varying storage temperatures, allowing qualitative food freshness discrimination via naked-eye observation. The precise quantitative detection in real water and foodstuff was applied, and further verified by ICP-MS, confirmed the excellent accuracy and environmental tolerance. This work presented an intelligent strategy for designing cost-effective, high-performance multivariate probes, holding significant promise for advancing food safety and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: A dual-signal sensor for highly selective and reliable detection of rutin based on molecularly imprinted Prussian blue analogue.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Xu J, Wang H, Bai H, Li J, Li H, Ma D
papers.abstract: The reliable and accurate quantification of rutin is essential for pharmaceutical quality control, pharmacokinetic investigations, and clinical applications, owing to its broad pharmacological activities. In this study, we address this need by developing a novel dual-mode sensing platform based on a molecularly imprinted polymer-coated bimetallic Prussian blue analogue (Mn/FePBA@MIP). The Mn/FePBA@MIP analogue not only exhibits high peroxidase-like catalytic activity via its synergistic bimetallic sites but also possesses target-specific recognition capability through its surface-imprinted cavities. Upon specific rebinding of rutin, the imprinted polymer layer blocks substrate access to the catalytic sites via a gatekeeper effect, thereby quenching both the colorimetric and fluorescent signals. Under optimized conditions, the developed sensor achieves wide linear detection ranges of 6-1536 μg mL-1 for the colorimetric mode and 6-3072 μg mL-1 for the fluorescent mode, with corresponding detection limits of 3.98 μg mL-1 and 1.32 μg mL-1, respectively. For on-site applications, the sensor was integrated with a smartphone-based readout system for quantitative analysis via RGB value extraction, and successfully applied to determine rutin in traditional Chinese medicine samples with satisfactory recoveries. This work thus provides a reliable and portable dual-signal strategy for routine quality assurance of rutin-related herbal products.

papers.title: HaloTag-directed magnetic immobilization of PAD4 for target-based screening of natural-product inhibitors.
papers.authors: Xu H, Zhu D, Zhao Z, Zuo H, Wang Y, Fang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Target-directed screening of bioactive natural products is often limited by the instability, poor recoverability, and repeated preparation requirements of soluble recombinant enzymes. Here, we developed a reusable magnetic peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) screening platform based on site-directed HaloTag immobilization. Recombinant Halo-PAD4 was captured directly from crude lysate by chloroalkane-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs-Cl) without an additional labor-intensive and time-consuming enzyme purification step, generating MNPs-Halo-PAD4 with retained catalytic activity and inhibitor responsiveness. Compared with soluble PAD4, the immobilized enzyme showed improved activity retention during storage and temperature exposure and could be magnetically recovered for repeated assays. The platform was applied to screen water, 75% ethanol, and ethyl acetate extracts of 15 traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) materials. Among the tested materials, Alpinia officinarum consistently exhibited the strongest PAD4-inhibitory activity in both soluble and immobilized PAD4 assays. Activity-guided high-performance liquid chromatography fractionation localized the inhibitory activity to fraction F3. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry tentatively annotated 13 constituents, and authentic-standard testing prioritized galangin. Galangin inhibited PAD4 with an IC50 value of 46.6 μM and showed direct interaction with PAD4 by biolayer interferometry, with an apparent KD of 7.8 μM. Molecular docking further provided a structural hypothesis for the interaction. This workflow combines HaloTag-chloroalkane chemistry, magnetic enzyme immobilization, liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry for the screening of PAD4 inhibitors. This proposed one-step capture and immobilization of recombinant protein also supports ligand screening for other protein targets.

papers.title: UWMT-net: An uncertainty-weighted multi-task network for ultrasound-based three-class classification of thyroid nodules.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.authors: Li Q, Mao Z, He Y, Wang J, Yang Z
papers.abstract:
Risk stratification of thyroid nodules on ultrasound remains inconsistent in routine practice, particularly for borderline presentations. Many deep-learning studies report discrimination alone, while probability reliability and threshold-based clinical utility receive less attention.
We retrospectively included 364 development patients, each contributing one thyroid nodule labeled using surgical histopathology or fine-needle aspiration cytology. The primary analysis used a patient-level fixed training/validation/test framework, and robustness was additionally assessed with stratified patient-level five-fold cross-validation. A locked model was independently evaluated in 121 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (Shandong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine), Jinan, China. The task was formulated as three-class classification: benign, indeterminate or suspicious, and malignant.
The multimodal model outperformed clinical-only and image-only baselines, with the largest gains observed on class-balanced metrics. On the held-out test set, UWMT-Net achieved an accuracy of 0.838 and a macro-AUC of 0.943. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced ECE from 0.040 to 0.015 without changing hard-label metrics. Five-fold cross-validation yielded a macro-AUC of 0.936 ± 0.011. In the independent external cohort, the locked model achieved an accuracy of 0.810, macro-F1 of 0.804, macro-AUC of 0.921, and ECE of 0.031. The added fusion baselines and paired bootstrap analysis supported a modest, but not statistically significant, numerical advantage of uncertainty-weighted multi-task learning.
Integrating ultrasound with structured clinical information improved three-class classification and probability reliability in the development cohort, with retained performance in the independent external cohort. Larger prospective multicenter validation remains required before clinical use.

papers.title: ZeXieYin formula attenuates trimethylamine N-oxide- induced atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment by regulating microglial-neuronal signaling and autophagy.
papers.authors: Wu W, He Y, Zhang X, Zhou S, Song Z, Hu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
ZeXieYin Formula (ZXYF), a classic traditional Chinese medicine decoction first documented in the Huangdi Neijing (an ancient Chinese medical text), traditionally used to treat patterns of internal accumulation of phlegm turbidity and deficiency of healthy qi-a pathogenesis closely associated with atherosclerosis and cognitive impairment, and which is composed of three medicinal herbs-Alisma plantago-aquatica L. (Zexie, Water Plantain Rhizome, dried tuber), Atractylodis macrocephala Koidz. (Baizhu, Largehead Atractylodes Rhizome, dried rhizome), and Pyrola calliantha Andres. (Luxiancao, Chinese Pyrola Herb, whole herb)-in a 2:2:1 ratio. For the preparation of ZXYF decoction, Zexie (200 g), Baizhu (200 g), and Luxiancao (100 g) were accurately weighed. ZXYF has been observed in our previous studies to reduce trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) levels, exert anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering effects and alleviate atherosclerosis (AS) while improving cognitive function.
To investigate whether ZXYF ameliorates TMAO-induced AS with concurrent cognitive impairment (AS-CI) by modulating microglia-mediated paracrine signaling and subsequent neuroinflammation.
To create an AS-CI model in vivo, Apolipoprotein E-deficient mice(ApoE-/- mice) were given a high-fat diet (containing the TMAO precursor choline) for 8 weeks. ZXYF (6.5, 13 g/kg) was administered via gavage. Aortic plaques were evaluated by Oil Red O staining, cognitive function was detected by behavioral tests (Y-maze, Morris water maze, and novel object recognition), and TMAO levels in brain tissue and serum were examined by Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-ESI-MS/MS). Immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were used to evaluate microglial activation, C-C chemokine receptor type 5 (CCR5) expression, microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) expression, toxic proteins deposition, and autophagic ultrastructure in the hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Western blot were performed to detect the protein expression of chemokines, factors that promote inflammation, and related signaling pathways. In vitro, a paracrine model of BV2 microglia and HT22 neurons was established, and autophagic flux was detected by transfection with green fluorescent protein-red fluorescent protein-LC3 (GFP-RFP-LC3) lentivirus. CCR5 antagonist maraviroc, mTOR inhibitor rapamycin, and ZXYF-containing serum were used for intervention to verify the signaling pathway mechanism.
ZXYF treatment significantly reduced aortic plaque area, enhanced working, spatial, and recognition memory (p < 0.05), and concurrently lowered TMAO levels in both brain tissue and serum. ZXYF prevented hippocampus microglial activation and the MAPK/NF-κB inflammatory cascade, and downregulated the release of proinflammatory factors. Mechanistic studies showed that ZXYF markedly reduced the expression of chemokines C-C motif chemokine ligand 3 (CCL3), C-C motif chemokine ligand 4 (CCL4) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) in the brain, inhibited the expression of their receptor CCR5 and downstream mTOR phosphorylation, thereby restoring neuronal autophagy (increasing the number of autophagosomes, upregulating LC3-II and Beclin1, and downregulating sequestosome 1 (p62)) and reducing the deposition of amyloid-beta (Aβ) and phosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) proteins. In vitro experiments supported that the conditioned medium of activated microglia induced autophagy inhibition and neuroinflammation through the CCL3/4/5-CCR5-mTOR axis, while maraviroc, rapamycin and ZXYF-containing serum could block this effect and restore autophagic flux.
ZXYF ameliorates AS-CI by reducing TMAO levels, inhibiting microglial activation and the release of CCL3/4/5, thereby blocking the neuronal CCR5-mTOR signaling axis, restoring autophagic function and alleviating neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
papers.authors: Yan K, Guo PX, Liang QY, Xu PT, Jin T, Chen LY et al.
papers.abstract:
Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown.
To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition.
A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release.
Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice.
This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

papers.title: Novel dissolving microneedles incorporating natural carrier-free self-assembled nanoparticles synergized with electroacupuncture for diabetic wound healing.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zeng Y, Zeng H, Huo H, Zeng M, Li M et al.
papers.abstract: Diabetic wounds (DW) are one of the most common complications of diabetes with complex pathogenesis, causing high morbidity and disability. Conventional therapies fail to resolve multiple obstacles to DW healing, urgently requiring efficient and safe novel interventions. Compounds from medicine and food homology substances have attracted widespread attention owing to their superior biosafety and diverse pharmacological activities. Herein, carrier-free APC and GQS nanoparticles were manufactured separately via self-assembly using medicine and food homology bioactive components, including astragalus polysaccharide, chlorogenic acid, quercetin, β-sitosterol, and glycyrrhizin acid. Subsequently, dissolvable APC@GQS@MNs co-loaded with APC and GQS were constructed using polyvinylpyrrolidone, hyaluronic acid, and aloe vera as matrix materials. Physicochemical characterization confirmed that APC@GQS@MNs have a well-defined conical morphology, satisfactory mechanical strength, and favorable skin penetration. The APC@GQS@MNs also enabled efficient selective scavenging of cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS), while physiological ROS were less affected. Meanwhile, APC@GQS@MNs exhibited favorable biocompatibility, reduced intracellular ROS levels, ameliorated oxidative stress-induced damage to cell proliferation, migration and tube formation, promoted M1 to M2 macrophage polarization, and effectively inhibited the growth and biofilm formation of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. In vivo results showed that APC@GQS@MNs promoted collagen deposition, re-epithelialization, and reduced local inflammatory infiltration in DW by upregulating CD31, CD163, IL-10 and suppressing iNOS, NF-κB, and TNF-α signaling. Notably, APC@GQS@MNs combined with electroacupuncture exerted synergistic effects, which further ameliorated the wound microenvironment and markedly accelerated wound healing and tissue regeneration. Such synergistic therapy modulates local wound states and inflammatory responses, laying a promising foundation for the management of DW.

papers.title: A GelMA hydrogel co-loaded with ursolic acid, ferulic acid and naringin facilitates dentin regeneration by providing a multi-component odontogenic microenvironment.
papers.authors: Che J, Yang A, Mo F, Gao Y, Li Y, Cui Y et al.
papers.abstract: Dental caries is a prevalent bacterial infectious disease, yet current clinical treatments remain limited because conventional restorative materials provide only mechanical filling and fail to induce dental tissue regeneration. Herein, we developed a composite gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel system (Gel/UFN) co-loaded with three active components from traditional Chinese medicine, including ursolic acid (UA), ferulic acid (FA) and naringin (Nar), to remodel the carious microenvironment and promote dentin remineralization and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation. Gel/UFN showed excellent biocompatibility and favorable physicochemical and mechanical properties for dental applications, supporting adhesion and proliferation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). Functionally, Gel/UFN significantly inhibited Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) growth and biofilm formation, downregulated inflammatory cytokine expression and promoted the migration and angiogenesis of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). More importantly, Gel/UFN upregulated odontogenesis-related genes in hDPSCs, thereby enhancing odontogenic differentiation, alkaline phosphatase activity, collagen maturation and regenerative mineralization. In vivo, Gel/UFN exhibited slow degradation and sustained drug release for over 55 days. After implantation of Gel/UFN-filled dentin discs into nude mice, H&E staining demonstrated the formation of vascular structures, dentin-like mineralized tissue and cell-rich pulp-like tissue. Western blot analysis further revealed increased expression of the odontogenesis-related proteins RUNX2, DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1 in the Gel/UFN group, providing additional protein-level evidence of its pro-odontogenic effects in vivo. These newly formed tissues were observed to cover exposed dentinal tubules on the surface of dentin disc using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Micro-CT further confirmed that dental tissue induced by Gel/UFN exhibited a higher remineralization density at the defect site, supporting enhanced dentin remineralization. Overall, Gel/UFN may serve as a promising bioactive hydrogel platform for dentin repair and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation through antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic and pro-differentiation effects.

papers.title: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework reveals mechanistic insights of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in ischemic stroke with experimental validation.
papers.authors: Qiao R, Liu C, Pan X, Tian Q, He F
papers.abstract:
Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD), a classical formula recorded in Yilin Gaicuo, has been widely used for the treatment of stroke and post-stroke sequelae in traditional Chinese medicine.
This study aims to establish a novel framework based on the EWMCRITIC-VIKOR algorithm to prioritize potential BYHWD targets against IS by integrating multi-dimensional biological features, with validation through in vivo experiments.
14 biological features across 4 dimensions were quantified. Feature weights were calculated using EWM and CRITIC, and integrated via VIKOR for MCDM on BYHWD-IS overlapping targets. The therapeutic effects of BYHWD were validated in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model. Anti-inflammatory effects were assessed by RT-qPCR and ELISA, while western blotting were used to evaluate signaling via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway.
The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework prioritized 5 key targets (FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, and IL6) from 239 overlapping targets. The VIKOR compromise solution exhibited a distinct low-Q priority set, in which the top targets jointly minimized group utility and individual regret, and the overall ranking showed weak association with logFC, indicating that prioritization was not driven by expression effect size alone. BYHWD treatment significantly improved MCAO-induced brain injury. RT-qPCR and ELISA showed marked downregulation of IL1B and IL6 after BYHWD treatment, and western blotting indicated altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling status.
The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework enables robust prioritization of therapeutic targets by integrating heterogeneous biological data. This approach enhances mechanistic understanding of BYHWD in IS and offers a reliable strategy for target discovery in herbal interventions.

papers.title: Integrated UPLC-Q-TOF and serum pharmacological analysis: Yinchenhao decoction alleviates alcoholic steatohepatitis via inhibition of COX-2/PI3K/Akt and suppression of M1 macrophage polarization.
papers.authors: Wen J, Zeng Q, Wang Y, Chen T, Xie S, Kuang S et al.
papers.abstract:
Yinchenhao decoction (YCHD), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula, has been widely used for the treatment of liver disorders. However, its therapeutic efficacy in alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
To systematically evaluate the protective effects of YCHD and its bioactive compounds against ASH and elucidate the potential mechanisms through an integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF analysis and network pharmacology, with particular emphasis on the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway and macrophage polarization.
The therapeutic effects of YCHD on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress, and inflammation were comprehensively evaluated using multiple experimental models. The chemical composition and material basis of YCHD were characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF analysis. Network pharmacology was subsequently employed to predict potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with the anti-ASH effects of YCHD. The regulatory effects of YCHD on macrophage polarization and the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway were further investigated through COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib and COX-2 siRNA. Finally, the major active compounds were screened and experimentally validated in zebrafish, AML12 cells, and RAW264.7 cells.
YCHD exerted protective effects across multiple experimental models by improving lipid metabolic disorders, reducing hepatic lipid accumulation, and alleviating inflammatory responses. Phytochemical profiling identified 1,740 compounds in YCHD, including 195 blood-absorbed components. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that the PI3K/Akt pathway represents a critical target underlying the therapeutic effects of YCHD. Further validation demonstrated that YCHD reduced the expression of macrophage M1 polarization markers CD80/CD86 and decreased the production of inflammatory cytokines in ASH mice. Consistently, YCHD serum exerted comparable protective effects in LPS-stimulated polarized RAW264.7 cells by suppressing the activation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. Pharmacological screening further identified acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin as potential key compounds.
YCHD effectively ameliorates ASH by restoring lipid homeostasis, mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressing M1 macrophage polarization through modulation of the COX-2/PI3K/Akt pathway. Acacetin, apigenin, and fisetin may represent important bioactive constituents contributing to the therapeutic effects of YCHD. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the pharmacological basis of YCHD in ASH treatment and establish a foundation for further identification and isolation of its active compounds.

papers.title: Development and validation of an LC-MS/MS method for the determination of mycotoxins in the medicinal and edible herb dandelion.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
papers.authors: Wang G, Tian C, Jiao M, Wang Y, Zhang X, Mohamed SR et al.
papers.abstract: Dandelion (Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.-Mazz.) is a medicinal and edible herb widely used in traditional Chinese medicine; however, studies on mycotoxin contamination in dandelion remain limited. Herein, we developed a liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-QqQ-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of five common mycotoxins: aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), deoxynivalenol (DON), fumonisin B1 (FB1), ochratoxin A (OTA), and zearalenone (ZEN) in dandelion. The mycotoxins were extracted from dandelion herb, cleaned up by solvent dilution, and analyzed in multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode on an LC-QqQ-MS/MS system. Key parameters were optimized to achieve the best performance, including chromatographic conditions, MRM ion pairs, extraction solvents, and sample cleanup methods. Method validation was conducted in terms of specificity, limit of determination, limit of quantitation, linearity, intraday and interday precision, and matrix effect. Finally, a total of 54 dandelion samples collected from different regions of China were analyzed using the developed method. AFB1 and FB1 were detected in all the dandelion samples, while OTA was found in 45 samples. DON was detected in nine samples from three regions, whereas ZEN was not detected in any of the samples. FB1 was found to be the most prevalent mycotoxin in the samples, ranging from 9.77 to 35.86 μg/kg, followed by AFB1 and OTA, indicating co-occurrence of mycotoxins in this herb.

papers.title: Jinfeng pills ameliorate levonorgestrel-induced ovarian injury by modulating ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and PI3K/Akt signaling.
papers.authors: Hu Y, Li G, Ni Q, Zhong R, Zhou J, Guo X et al.
papers.abstract:
Jinfeng Pills (JFP, NMPA approval No. Z20064400) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used to regulate menstruation and support ovulation. It consists of nine medicinal materials: Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. (Yinyanghuo), Cervus elaphus Linnaeus (Lurong), Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. (Renshen), Equus asinus (EJiao), Ligustrum lucidum W.T.Aiton (Nvzhenzi), Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke (Heshouwu), Curculigo orchioides Gaertn (Xianmao), Cinnamomum cassia (L.). J.Presl (Rougui) and Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Yimucao). Previous studies have demonstrated the protective effects of JFP against ovarian dysfunction. However, the potential protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic exposure to levonorgestrel (LNG), a progestin commonly used in emergency contraception, and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic LNG exposure and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.
A rat model of chronic LNG exposure was established, and the efficacy of JFP was evaluated based on estrous cycles, serum hormone levels and ovarian morphology. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis and cholesterol-related biochemical assays were performed to investigate the alterations in ovarian cholesterol homeostasis. The role of apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA1) was further examined by using ApoA1 silencing in primary rat ovarian theca cells and intrabursal administration of ApoA1 in vivo. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were subsequently used to validate the key molecular changes and assess the effects of JFP on ApoA1expression, cholesterol homeostasis and the associated signaling pathways.
JFP significantly ameliorated LNG-induced ovarian injury, as evidenced by increased serum levels of FSH, LH and AMH, and decreased estradiol levels and the LH/FSH ratio, reduced cystic follicle formation, and attenuated follicular depletion. Transcriptomic analysis in ovarian tissues, together with cholesterol assays, RT-qPCR and Western blotting, revealed that LNG exposure disrupted ovarian cholesterol homeostasis, with alterations in cholesterol transport and increased ovarian ApoA1 abundance. Intrabursal administration of ApoA1 induced ovarian pathological changes and activated PI3K/Akt signaling in vivo, whereas ApoA1 silencing attenuated PI3K/Akt activation and inhibited the viability of primary ovarian theca cells. JFP markedly reduced ovarian ApoA1 accumulation, improved cholesterol homeostasis, and suppressed PI3K/Akt/NF-κB signaling.
JFP effectively ameliorated ovarian injury induced by long-term LNG exposure in rats, and its protective effects were likely associated with modulation of ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and suppression of PI3K/Akt signaling.

papers.title: Chaihu-Shugan-San attenuates depression by downregulating liver LCN2 to suppress LHb GluN2B-associated glutamatergic signaling.
papers.authors: You X, Song C, Chen W, Zheng Y, Wang R, Liu W et al.
papers.abstract:
The liver-brain axis has emerged as a critical pathway in depression pathogenesis, yet the molecular basis of this crosstalk remains largely unexplored. Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula for "soothing the liver and relieving depression" has shown both hepatoprotective and antidepressant effects, but whether these actions are linked via the liver-brain axis and through what molecular mechanism remains unknown.
This study aimed to determine whether CSS exerts antidepressant effects via the liver-brain axis and to elucidate the mediating role of liver lipocalin 2 (LCN2) and its receptor SLC22A17 in regulating lateral habenula (LHb) function.
A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established. CSS (2, 4, 8 g/kg) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) was orally administered. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed by sucrose preference, open field, and forced swim tests. Hepatic injury was evaluated by serum ALT/AST and H&E staining. Liver transcriptomics and LHb single-cell RNA sequencing were performed to identify key molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, ELISA, and immunofluorescence for validation. The causal role of LCN2 was tested via liver-specific AAV-mediated overexpression.
CSS ameliorated CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors and liver injury. Transcriptomics and PPI network analysis identified Lcn2 as a hub gene. CSS reversed CUMS-induced elevation of LCN2 in the liver, serum, and LHb, as well as the upregulation of its receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb. LHb single-cell sequencing revealed that CSS restored CUMS-induced changes in astrocyte subcluster ASC6, including downregulation of AQP4 and SLC38A1 and impaired intercellular communication. Consequently, CSS reduced the elevated expression of c-FOS and GluN2B and restored AQP4 and SLC38A1 in the LHb. Importantly, liver-specific Lcn2 overexpression recapitulated CUMS-like depressive phenotypes and LHb abnormalities, including elevated SLC22A17 and GluN2B, and largely abolished the antidepressant effects of CSS.
CSS ameliorates depressive-like behaviors in association with downregulation of hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb, restoring ASC6-mediated glutamate homeostasis, and suppressing GluN2B-related Glutamatergic Signaling. These findings are consistent with a model in which LHb function may be modulated via the liver-brain axis through hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17, although the direct source of LHb LCN2 remains to be determined, offering experimental support for the scientific basis of CSS in "soothing the liver and relieving depression."

papers.title: Siwu Paste alleviates blood deficiency syndrome induced by cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine in association with gut microbiota remodeling and improved splenic metabolic homeostasis.
papers.authors: Wan D, Feng X, Xu S, Du Q, Yue W, Zhang S
papers.abstract:
Siwu Paste (SWP), derived from the classical blood-tonifying formula Siwu Decoction, has long been used for blood deficiency-related disorders and has a well-established traditional basis and ethnopharmacological value. Blood deficiency syndrome (BDS) is a common syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine and is associated with impaired blood generation and hematopoietic dysfunction. However, the modern pharmacological mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of SWP on BDS remain incompletely understood.
This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic effects of SWP on cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine induced BDS and to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying its improvement of hematopoietic function.
The chemical constituents of SWP were characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS), and its potential mechanisms were predicted using network pharmacology. An acetylphenylhydrazine (APH)/cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced BDS rat model was used to evaluate SWP efficacy through flow cytometry, histology, Western blotting, qPCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and exogenous adenosine diphosphate (ADP) supplementation experiments were performed to evaluate the contribution of the gut microbiota and the involvement of splenic ADP-related metabolic alterations.
SWP significantly improved hematopoietic dysfunction, alleviated systemic inflammation, restored intestinal barrier integrity, reversed the Treg/Th17 imbalance, and reduced apoptosis within the CD45+CD34+ bone marrow cell population in BDS rats. Multi-omics analysis revealed that SWP significantly regulated gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles; specifically, SWP treatment was associated with a significant increase in the relative abundance of Allobaculum and an upward trend in Lactobacillus, accompanied by a significant reduction in the relative abundance of total ADP in spleen tissue compared with the BDS group. FMT experiments partially transferred the hematopoietic and immunomodulatory effects associated with SWP treatment. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment and exogenous ADP supplementation attenuated several SWP-induced improvements in bone-marrow hematopoietic function and Treg/Th17 balance, consistent with the involvement of the gut microbiota-splenic metabolic axis in the therapeutic effects of SWP.
SWP alleviates bone marrow hematopoietic dysfunction in BDS rats, with these effects accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation, and improved metabolic homeostasis. These findings provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional TCM concept of "treating the marrow via the gut" in blood deficiency-related disorders.

papers.title: Sinensetin inhibits choroidal neovascularization by downregulating the MAPK/ERK pathway.
papers.authors: Han GJ, Du Y, Wu XX, He YX, Lu J, Wang WJ et al.
papers.abstract:
Sinensetin (SIN), a characteristic polymethoxyflavone abundant in Citrus species, is isolated from Citrus peel (Chenpi), a medicinal material widely applied in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) to activate blood circulation and ameliorate blood stasis-associated ocular disorders. Accumulating pharmacological evidence confirms that SIN exerts prominent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic bioactivities. It is capable of suppressing pathological angiogenesis in zebrafish and endothelial cell models, which renders SIN a promising candidate for angiogenic ocular diseases. Nevertheless, its therapeutic efficacy against choroidal neovascularization (CNV) remains largely uninvestigated.
This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effects of SIN on CNV and to dissect the underlying mechanism, specifically focusing on its modulation of FGF1-mediated MAPK/ERK signaling.
The anti-CNV effect of SIN was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo. In vivo, a laser-induced CNV model was established in Brown Norway (BN) rats, and SIN was administered via intravitreal injection; CNV severity was assessed by FITC perfusion, OCT, HE staining, and Western blot. In vitro, human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) were treated with CNV-mimicking ARPE-19 human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) conditioned medium; the effects of SIN on migration and angiogenesis were evaluated by scratch, transwell, and tube formation assays. Combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were employed to screen key targets and pathways, and mechanistic validation was performed using the ERK agonist PMA and inhibitor U0126.
In the laser-induced CNV rat model, intravitreal injection of SIN significantly reduced CNV area and thickness and suppressed the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, effects that were reversed by the ERK agonist PMA. Consistently, in vitro experiments confirmed that SIN dose-dependently reversed the enhanced migration and tube formation of HUVEC induced by CNV-mimicking conditioned medium. Multi-omics analysis identified FGF1 as a shared candidate downstream mediator of SIN, with SIN downregulating FGF1, VEGF-A, HIF-1α, and p-ERK1/2 expression. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the ERK inhibitor U0126 mimicked the anti-angiogenic effect of SIN, whereas the ERK agonist PMA abolished its inhibitory activity, suggesting that SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling.
Collectively, this study demonstrates that citrus-derived SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling, while additional pathways identified by multi-omics may also contribute. These findings highlight SIN as a promising natural product for the treatment of CNV-related ocular diseases, with FGF1 identified as a potential mediator underlying its anti-angiogenic action.

papers.title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Tan W, Wang C, Liu X, Deng J, Sang Z, Hu X
papers.abstract:
Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula.
To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects.
ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR.
BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice.
BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

papers.title: Mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine-derived active components in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease: A comprehensive review.
papers.authors: Tian Y, Guo J, Lin X, Zhang F, Xie J, Hou X et al.
papers.abstract:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and multifactorial pathology. Because AD involves interacting pathological processes, the limited efficacy of conventional single-target therapies has increased interest in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and other natural medicines with multi-target pharmacological actions. TCM-derived active components originate from medicinal materials used in traditional practice and are evaluated using modern pharmacological approaches. Their source medicines have diverse traditional-use backgrounds. Some have historical associations with memory or cognitive symptoms, whereas many others were traditionally used for broader deficiency, phlegm, blood-stasis, heat, or related syndromic patterns. These records provide ethnopharmacological context for the source medicines but should not be taken as historical evidence for the anti-AD activity of their isolated constituents.
This review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms of TCM-derived bioactive components in AD while incorporating relevant traditional-use information on their source medicines. Particular attention is given to their multi-target actions and emerging mechanisms involving ferroptosis, mitophagy, and the gut-brain axis.
Mechanistic literature published between January 2019 and November 2025 was retrieved from Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Ovid MEDLINE and PubMed were searched separately to maximize retrieval across indexed and additional PubMed records, with overlapping records removed during deduplication. Traditional-use information was evaluated separately for the source medicines. A targeted search of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov was also conducted to assess human interventional evidence for compounds covered in the review, with trial-registration information updated through August 2026.
Current preclinical findings suggest that TCM active components may produce coordinated preclinical pharmacological effects through multiple pathways, including the inhibition of β-amyloid (Aβ) production and deposition, regulation of tau aggregation and phosphorylation, alleviation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, improvement of mitophagy and iron metabolism disorders, and modulation of gut microbiota homeostasis. Among these components, saponins show broad mechanistic coverage. Flavonoids, polysaccharides, and other bioactive substances have likewise shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, together with protective effects on synaptic function, in preclinical models. These mechanistic findings were derived predominantly from cellular and animal studies, with computational analyses providing mainly hypothesis-generating support. Human evidence was available for only a small subset of compounds and was not uniformly positive. Huperzine A has progressed to controlled clinical testing but has shown mixed efficacy findings; resveratrol demonstrated CNS exposure and biomarker activity without consistent cognitive benefit; curcumin did not show efficacy in a placebo-controlled AD trial; and favorable signals from ginseng studies were limited by open-label designs and the use of whole preparations rather than isolated ginsenosides.
The available evidence supports broad preclinical activity of TCM-derived components across several interconnected AD-related processes, but the strength of mechanistic support varies markedly among compounds and pathways. Human translation remains limited and inconsistent, and current clinical data do not establish disease-modifying efficacy for the compounds reviewed. Further development should therefore be guided by the main uncertainty surrounding each candidate-whether mechanistic causality, reproducibility, systemic or CNS exposure, preparation standardization, or clinical efficacy-rather than by a fixed sequence of technologies.

papers.title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
papers.authors: Wang J, Ma S, Yu D, Wang Y, Ma C, Ma D et al.
papers.abstract:
Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection.
SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model.
Among 1991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection.
This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

papers.title: Schisandrin B attenuates the platelet activation-thrombosis cascade through inhibition of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT and extracellular signal-regulated kinase-talin-mediated integrin αIIbβ3 signaling.
papers.authors: Li M, Liu Z, Shen Y, Li Q, Wen K, Gu X et al.
papers.abstract:
Schisandrin B (Sch B), a principal bioactive lignan derived from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill., Exhibits diverse pharmacological activities. This traditional Chinese medicine possesses therapeutic value for treating symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and a faint, nearly imperceptible pulse caused by deficiency of both qi and yin.
This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch B on platelet activation and thrombosis, employing a combination of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and comprehensive in vitro and in vivo functional assays.
Platelet aggregation and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) release were assessed using a lumi-aggregometer. Flow cytometry was used to evaluate Sch B's effects on P-selectin expression and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Platelet adhesion, spreading, and clot retraction assays were performed to analyze outside-in signaling. Potential targets and signaling pathways of Sch B were predicted through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and these predictions were further investigated using Western blot analysis. In vivo, the effects of Sch B on thrombus formation were evaluated using murine models.
Sch B significantly suppressed platelet aggregation, granule release, adhesion, spreading, P-selectin expression, and PAC-1 binding. Western blot further analysis revealed that Sch B reduced the phosphorylation of key signaling molecules, such as Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), AKT, Extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK), Talin1, and β3 integrin. In a mesenteric arterial thrombosis model induced by ferric chloride (FeCl3), Sch B significantly prolonged the time to stable thrombus formation. However, it did not significantly affect coagulation parameters or tail-bleeding time in mice.
Sch B inhibits platelet activation by interfering with the PI3K/AKT/ERK-Talin signaling pathway, thereby attenuating thrombus formation. This supports its potential as an antiplatelet agent with a favorable safety profile.

papers.title: Platycodon Decoction alleviates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease associated inflammation with potential dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.
papers.authors: Luan H, Yu M, Wang T, Ji H, Tseng Y
papers.abstract:
The traditional Chinese medicine formula Platycodon Decoction (PD) is known to be effective to alleviate respiratory system-related symptoms, its effect and integrated mechanism for treating COPD requires elucidation.
This study aims to systematically address the pharmacology of PD in treating COPD through analyzing how PD inhibiting the intracellular inflammatory pathway and intercellular interactions.
PD composition was ascertained via LC-MS/MS. PD-induced organ damage was assessed through an acute toxicity test. Following the intervention of PD, body weight, lung index, sputum volume, pulmonary function, expression of inflammatory factors, pulmonary tissue injury, mucus secretion, and MUC5AC expression of the COPD-modeled mice were measured. PD's impacts on the levels of inflammatory factors, cellular activity, proliferation, cell cycle, reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and inter-cellular communication were assessed through Beas-2b human bronchus epithelial cells and THP-1 human macrophage. The PD-associated, COPD relevant inflammatory pathways were analyzed through network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics and then verified through Western blots. The involved cells for cell receptor identified by network pharmacology was analyzed by single-cell sequencing and verified by molecular dynamics and Western blot.
The acute toxicity assessment provided preliminary evidence of PD tolerability under the tested conditions. Fifty compounds were identified in PD. Animal experiments demonstrated that PD can decrease the inflammatory levels and alleviate excessive mucus secretion in mice. In vitro cell experiments indicated that PD can efficiently abate inflammation and oxidative stress within the COPD-related airway microenvironment and diminish epithelial-macrophage interactions. Integration of single-cell and network pharmacology analyses identified ADGRE5 as a candidate receptor that may mediate epithelial-macrophage interactions. PD treatment reduced PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and was accompanied by decreased ADGRE5 expression.
PD alleviates inflammation in COPD, potentially involving dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.

papers.title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.authors: Li Q, Liu Y, Zhou Z, Huang Y, Deng L, Ye Y
papers.abstract:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated.
To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation.
The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF.
HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA.
SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

papers.title: Methyl jasmonate induces the biosynthesis and accumulation of triterpenoid saponins in Polygala tenuifolia hairy roots.
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.authors: Ji H, Yang B, Lai N, Zhang L, Yang Y, Zhao X et al.
papers.abstract: Polygala tenuifolia Willd. is an important medicinal plant widely applied in traditional Chinese medicine. Its pharmacological activities are primarily derived from triterpenoid saponins and other specialized metabolites. Nevertheless, the regulatory mechanisms governing methyl jasmonate (MeJA)-triggered accumulation of bioactive constituents in P. tenuifolia remain poorly characterized. In this study, to evaluate corresponding changes in biomass and characteristic metabolite production, hairy root cultures of P. tenuifolia were subjected to MeJA treatment at concentrations spanning 0-400 µM over a 1-6 day period. MeJA modulated hairy root growth and secondary metabolite accumulation in a concentration-dependent and time-dependent manner. Compared with the control group, the contents of onjisaponin B and polygalasaponin III increased by 1.81-fold and 2.60-fold, respectively, following treatment with 50 µM MeJA for 3 days. A total of 447 differentially expressed transcription factors (TFs) that belonged to 64 families were identified through transcriptome analysis. MeJA suppressed the expression of most TF families, whereas the NAC family exhibited a global upregulation trend. The above results indicated that MeJA activated transcriptional reprogramming of secondary-metabolism-associated genes via targeted regulation of specific TFs. Correlation analysis involving ten key enzyme genes and six characteristic metabolites demonstrated that the majority of biosynthetic genes were positively associated with bioactive metabolite levels. Of these genes, UGT74B1 and UGT73B2 showed strong positive correlations with multiple saponin components; CYP94A2 served as a critical node responsible for oxidative modification. In contrast, MK and HDS displayed negative correlations with saponins, which suggested precursor competition across distinct terpenoid pathways. As indicated by RT-qPCR validation for ten candidate biosynthetic genes, MeJA time-dependently upregulated key genes participating in the MVA/MEP pathways, squalene cyclization, CYP450-mediated oxidation, and UGT-catalyzed glycosylation, thereby facilitating precursor supply and subsequent structural modification. Accordingly, triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis and accumulation in P. tenuifolia hairy roots were enhanced. This study offers fresh understanding of the molecular basis underlying MeJA-modulated secondary metabolism in P. tenuifolia, and identifies candidate genes applicable to metabolic engineering for elevating yields of bioactive compounds in hairy root cultures.

papers.title: Yupingfeng alleviates allergic rhinitis by modulating gut microbiota and succinate to inhibit mTOR/S6K signaling.
papers.authors: Zuo Y, Li Y, Huang Z, Zeng H, Liu Q, Zhou Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Yupingfeng granules (YPF), derived from the classic traditional Chinese medicine prescription Yupingfeng powder, have been recommended in clinical practice guidelines for the management of allergic rhinitis (AR), and their clinical efficacy is widely recognized. However, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms have not been thoroughly investigated.
This study aimed to investigate whether YPF protects the nasal epithelial barrier and alleviates AR by modulating the gut microbiota and pathways related to its metabolites.
An OVA-induced AR mouse model was established and phenotypically evaluated. The dependence of YPF efficacy on gut microbiota was assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, antibiotic depletion, and fecal microbiota transplantation. 1H-NMR metabolomics was used to identify key metabolites, followed by exogenous supplementation for validation. Nasal mucosal transcriptome sequencing was performed to explore downstream pathways, and functional validation was conducted in OVA-induced HNEpCs through metabolite intervention, YPF co-treatment, mTOR knockdown, and MHY1485 treatment.
YPF dose-dependently reduced nasal rubbing and sneezing, attenuated IgE-mediated type 2 inflammation, and ameliorated nasal epithelial barrier injury in OVA-induced AR mice. YPF remodeled the gut microbiota and increased microbial diversity. Gut microbiota depletion attenuated the protective effects of YPF, whereas FMT from YPF donors reproduced them. Metabolomic analysis identified succinate as a key YPF-responsive metabolite, and exogenous succinate aggravated nasal epithelial barrier injury. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that succinate-induced nasal mucosal injury may involve mTOR signaling activation. In vitro, succinate aggravated OVA-induced barrier injury in HNEpCs, with disrupted Occludin distribution and enhanced mTOR/S6K phosphorylation, whereas YPF co-treatment reversed these changes. mTOR knockdown mimicked the protective effects of YPF, whereas MHY1485 attenuated them.
YPF alleviates OVA-induced AR by remodeling the gut microbiota, reducing succinate accumulation, and suppressing mTOR/S6K signaling to preserve nasal epithelial barrier integrity.

papers.title: Tongsai Granules ameliorate airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by remodeling LIPA-driven ceramide metabolism.
papers.authors: Cheng M, Li K, Zhang Z, Xin N, Liu X, Du Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear.
To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis.
A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed.
TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC.
TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

papers.title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Han Z, Zhao F, Xu H, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research.

papers.title: Ratiometric fluorescence determination of phoxim in traditional Chinese medicine matrices using Astragalus residue-derived carbon dots and rhodamine B.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Wang C, He X, Li X, Dong J, Zhang J, Shao P et al.
papers.abstract: An internally referenced fluorescence method was developed for the determination of phoxim in traditional Chinese medicine matrices. Astragalus residue-derived carbon quantum dots (AR-CQDs) were prepared from Astragalus residue and urea by one-step hydrothermal treatment and combined with Rhodamine B (RhB) to form a dual-emission probe. The AR-CQDs were quasi-spherical, with an average particle size of 4.02 nm, a fluorescence quantum yield of 10.33%, and abundant oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface groups. Under 320 nm excitation, the AR-CQDs emission at 413 nm served as the response signal, whereas the RhB emission at 580 nm served as the reference signal. Phoxim selectively attenuated the 413 nm emission, and F413/F580 was linearly related to phoxim concentration from 5 to 100 μM (R2 = 0.9952), with a detection limit of 0.106 μM after a 1 min incubation. UV-Vis absorption, fluorescence lifetime, inner-filter-effect correction, zeta-potential, and dynamic light-scattering results suggested that phoxim-induced surface interactions accompanied by aggregation-related effects contributed to the fluorescence attenuation, while the exact microscopic mechanism was not uniquely resolved.In Astragalus, red date, goji berry, and tap-water samples, recoveries were 96.90%-99.60% with RSDs of 1.72%-3.32%, and the results showed acceptable agreement with LC-MS/MS. The method provides a simple ratiometric approach for phoxim screening within the tested matrix and concentration ranges while enabling the analytical valorization of Astragalus residue.
